title: FoSA 第 4 章 · 架构特征定义：「-ility」们到底指什么 — 专业书籍精读 Book 211
title_en: FoSA Ch 4 · Architecture Characteristics Defined: What the -ilities Actually Mean — Book Deep Read 211

questions.question: 按 FoSA 第 4 章的三条判据，下面哪一项应当升格为架构特征？
options: 界面要好看统一，所有页面的配色、字体和按钮样式保持一致
接入第三方支付处理方，开发时按照常规的安全编码习惯来格外小心地处理
系统要支持用户在订单完成后七天内申请退款并原路退回款项
自己处理支付，需要把支付隔离成一个独立的模块或服务来专门防护
questions.explanation: 架构特征要同时满足：非领域的设计考量、影响结构、对成败关键。自建支付需要专门的结构来隔离，才过得了第二条；接第三方只需常规谨慎，不改变骨架；退款是领域需求；界面好看是设计问题，不改结构。
questions.question_en: By the three criteria in Chapter 4 of Fundamentals of Software Architecture, which of these should be promoted to an architecture characteristic?
options_en: Keeping the interface attractive and uniform, with consistent colors, fonts and buttons on every page
Integrating a third-party payment processor and handling it with the usual careful secure-coding habits
Letting users request a refund within seven days of an order and returning the money the way it came
Processing payments in-house, which calls for isolating payments in its own module or service for dedicated protection
questions.explanation_en: A characteristic must be a non-domain design consideration, affect structure, and be critical to success. In-house payments need dedicated structure to isolate them, so they pass the structural test; a third-party processor needs only normal care and leaves the skeleton unchanged; refunds are a domain requirement; looks are a design matter.

questions.question: 一家高频交易公司的需求文档里一个字都没提延迟。按本章的观点，架构师该怎么对待低延迟？
options: 把它当作隐式特征，靠领域知识识别出来并为之设计，即使文档没写
既然需求没写就不算架构特征，等业务方明确提出后再纳入设计
把它归入横切特征，和安全、合规一样交给统一的网关去处理
把它当作上线后的质量属性，等压测发现瓶颈再针对性地调优
questions.explanation: 隐式特征很少被写出来却是成功所必需；书里正是拿高频交易举例：那里每个系统都要为低延迟设计，差几毫秒就是钱。所以架构师需要领域知识去「听出」它；骨架几乎不能事后补，等上线再调优已经晚了。
questions.question_en: A high-frequency trading firm's requirements say nothing at all about latency. According to this chapter, how should the architect treat low latency?
options_en: As an implicit characteristic, identified through domain knowledge and designed for even though no document states it
As not an architecture characteristic, since it isn't written down; add it once the business asks for it explicitly
As a cross-cutting characteristic, handed to a shared gateway just like security and compliance
As a post-launch quality attribute, tuned once load testing reveals where the bottlenecks are
questions.explanation_en: Implicit characteristics are rarely written down yet essential to success, and the book uses exactly this example: in high-frequency trading every system must be designed for low latency because milliseconds are money. That's why architects need domain knowledge to hear them; the skeleton can hardly be retrofitted after launch.

questions.question: 架构评审上，团队列出 12 个「都很关键」的架构特征，希望每一个都做到最好。本章会怎么评价？
options: 特征互相牵制、各添复杂度，只挑少数关键的求「最不坏」，并让架构易改
应按 ISO 质量模型把 12 个都拆成子项逐一达标，就能得到真正最优的架构
列得越全越安全，漏掉一个特征的代价远高于多支持一个，所以 12 个都应保留
只要选对了技术栈，各个特征之间就不会冲突，可以同时把每一个都做到最好
questions.explanation: 本章最常被引用的话是：别追求最好的架构，要追求最不坏的。安全会拖累性能，像直升机的操纵杆动一个牵动其余；特征贪多会得到臃肿的通用怪物。既然很难一次选对，就让架构易于修改，降低选错的代价。
questions.question_en: At an architecture review the team lists 12 "all critical" characteristics and wants every one maximized. How would this chapter respond?
options_en: Characteristics pull against each other and each adds complexity; pick a few that matter, aim for least worst rather than best, and keep the architecture easy to change
Break all 12 into sub-characteristics per the ISO quality model and meet each one to reach a truly optimal architecture
The more complete the list the safer; missing a characteristic costs far more than supporting an extra one, so keep all 12
With the right technology stack the characteristics won't conflict, so every one of them can be maximized at once
questions.explanation_en: The chapter's best-known line: never aim for the best architecture, aim for the least worst. Security drags on performance, like helicopter controls where moving one moves the rest, and wanting everything yields a bloated generic design. Since getting it right the first time is hard, make the architecture easy to change so a wrong choice costs less.
